overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the committee did not deliberate on the vaguely noticed legal settlements topic, and the law does not require adding public-requested agenda items.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice topic "Discussion of Legal Settlements" under Superintendent's Report was too vague because it did not identify the specific legal matters.
allegations.key_passage: where a public body does not actually engage in any deliberation on a particular topic, it cannot violate the Open Meeting Law with respect to the sufficiency of the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to place on the agenda topics the complainant had asked to be discussed, such as safety concerns about a child.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law contains no requirement that a public body add topics to its meeting agenda if requested by members of the public.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
